item.title: Modeling of Chemically Reactive Gas Flows for Multi-Scale Problems
item.description: arXiv:2611.31330v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate modeling of chemical reactions plays a key role in the investigation of high-temperature flows. The Direct Simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) method provides highly accurate solutions for such flows. However, its computational cost becomes prohibitive for low Knudsen regimes. Particle-based continuum methods employing the Bhatnagar-Gross-Krook (BGK) or Fokker-Planck approximations have gained increasing attention in recent years, improve computational efficiency in low-Knudsen regimes by modeling relaxation processes rather than binary collisions, while retaining the particle approach that enables straightforward coupling with DSMC. In the last years, different continuum-based models in the open-source particle code PICLas have been extended to simulate gas mixtures with internal energy modes. The present work focuses on modeling of chemically reactive gas mixtures in the Ellipsoidal Statistical BGK model. Model accuracy is assessed for two test cases of a reactive gases confined in a reservoir.
item.dc:creator: Franziska Tuttas, Marcel Pfeiffer

item.title: Variance and Higher-Order Moments in Computational Fluctuating Hydrodynamics with Multiplicative Noise
item.description: arXiv:2611.31978v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fluctuating hydrodynamics (FHD) models mesoscopic fluid systems by augmenting classical conservation laws with stochastic flux terms governed by the fluctuation-dissipation theorem. While traditional validation of computational FHD (CFHD) algorithms focuses primarily on second-order central moments of equilibrium fluctuations, accurately resolving higher-order moments, such as skewness and kurtosis, is essential for evaluating non-linear functions of hydrodynamic fields. In this work, we analyze finite-volume CFHD discretizations to evaluate second-, third-, and fourth-order central moments of thermodynamic fluctuations. Using the one-dimensional stochastic heat equation, we demonstrate that incorporating multiplicative noise is necessary to recover the expected gamma distribution for temperature in the canonical ensemble, whereas additive noise models yield a Gaussian distribution that fails to capture non-zero skewness and excess kurtosis. We also derive analytical expressions for inherent modeling errors that persist in the limit of vanishing time step for a variety of boundary conditions. Furthermore, we introduce an improved formulation for Dirichlet boundary conditions that eliminates large boundary-adjacent errors in the third central moment present in traditional boundary treatments. We also examine higher-order temporal integration schemes, demonstrating that Stratonovich-based integrators, such as Heun's predictor-corrector method, can reduce these modeling errors. Finally, numerical simulations of the full compressible, stochastic Navier--Stokes equations confirm the generality and practical applicability of the findings obtained from the stochastic heat equation.
item.dc:creator: Satinderpreet Singh, Changho Kim, Ishan Srivastava, Andrew J. Nonaka, John B. Bell, Alejandro L. Garcia

item.title: Efficient spin-lattice dynamics and spin thermometry with machine-learned magnetic potentials
item.description: arXiv:2611.32129v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In finite-temperature spin-lattice dynamics, conventional force-only spin thermometers fail for energies nonlinear in each spin, while the standard semi-implicit SIB integrator requires two model evaluations per step. Here we introduce a geometric-probe spin temperature that is exact for arbitrary high-order smooth Hamiltonians using first-order spin forces alone without Hessians, making it naturally suited for nonlinear many-body machine-learning (ML) magnetic potentials. Complementarily, our cached-field integrator (CFI) stays second-order accurate with a single model evaluation per step, about halving the time per step with ML potentials. Extensive benchmarks against Monte Carlo across analytic and ML systems confirm both exact thermometry and accurate thermodynamics.
item.dc:creator: Yuanmai Zheng, Liangliang Hong, Xingao Gong, Hongjun Xiang, Hongyu Yu

item.title: First-principles phase diagram of monolayer CrS$_2$ polymorphs under biaxial strain and its sensitivity to the Hubbard U parameter
item.description: arXiv:2611.32265v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In correlated two-dimensional magnets the balance between competing electronic and magnetic phases is often set by the strength of the on-site Coulomb interaction, so that the predicted ground state can hinge on a parameter that is not uniquely defined. Monolayer CrS$_2$ lies squarely in this regime, hosting several energetically close polymorphs whose character ranges from non-magnetic semiconducting to magnetically ordered metallic. We therefore investigate, using DFT$+U$ within the generalized gradient approximation, the structural, magnetic, and electronic properties of the 1H, 1T, 1T$'$, and 1T$''$ polymorphs of monolayer CrS$_2$ under varying Hubbard interactions ($U=0$--$8$~eV) and biaxial strain ($-10\%$ to $+10\%$). The 1T-derived structures remain metallic and magnetic throughout, with $U$ acting mainly as a spectral renormalization. The 1H phase behaves differently, passing from a non-magnetic semiconductor through an antiferromagnetic semiconducting regime before metallizing, so that the gap closes as $U$ increases while the local Cr moment grows monotonically. Biaxial tensile strain at fixed $U$ induces a similar sequence of transitions. Along both tuning pathways, the two inequivalent nearest-neighbor Cr--Cr exchange channels progressively separate and cross, with the parallel-spin channel becoming dominant, accompanied by a breathing-type bond disproportionation. Independent calculations with a localized-orbital implementation reproduce the overall evolution but yield shifted critical values of $U$ and of strain, demonstrating the robustness of the phase diagram while highlighting the implementation dependence of the transition thresholds.
item.dc:creator: Rashmi Ranjan Routaray, Ali Ghojavand, Eric Bousquet

item.title: Neural-operator acceleration of bidirectional phonon Boltzmann-Fourier coupling for multiscale heat transport in silicon fin arrays
item.description: arXiv:2611.31542v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Localized heating in semiconductor devices can produce non-diffusive phonon transport near heat-generating regions, while heat spreading through the surrounding substrate remains well described by Fourier conduction. We present a hybrid framework that couples a pretrained neural operator for the phonon Boltzmann transport equation (BTE) within individual fins to a Fourier model of a shared substrate. To reduce the cost of repeated BTE solves across fin positions and coupling iterations, a DeepONet maps each fin's substrate-interface temperature and heating state to its temperature and heat-flux fields. The operator is trained on interface temperatures generated by a linearized proxy of the coupled problem, which avoids explicit training data collection from full coupled runs. An energy-balance penalty regularizes the learned operator, and a mixed finite-element formulation represents substrate heat flux in an H(div)-conforming space. The two models exchange temperature and normal heat flux through a non-overlapping Schwarz iteration with adaptive Aitken relaxation. We evaluate the framework on an idealized three-dimensional array of 100 silicon fins. For a held-out switching configuration, the neural-operator-Fourier solution differs from the direct BTE-Fourier reference by a maximum of 0.3 K in temperature and 0.6% in relative flux across all fins. Excluding the one-time substrate factorization, the coupled surrogate run takes about 50 s, compared with 2 h 28 min for direct coupling, a speedup of approximately 180x. Additional held-out switching patterns converge with the same trained operator. These results demonstrate neural-operator acceleration of bidirectional kinetic-continuum coupling for the tested geometry and material. This bidirectional strategy may extend to other multiscale materials problems coupling learned local neural models with continuum solvers.
item.dc:creator: Ruthwik Chivukula, Khemraj Shukla, George Em Karniadakis

item.title: Parton Physics in the Schwinger Model from Matrix Product States
item.description: arXiv:2611.31749v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Parton distribution functions (PDFs) and light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs) encode the non-perturbative structure of hadrons in terms of their partonic constituents. They are defined through matrix elements containing parton operators that are connected by a Wilson line along a light-front direction, which makes them difficult to access in Euclidean lattice calculations. We demonstrate how parton functions can be directly obtained in Minkowski space using the Hamiltonian framework. We compute fermion and antifermion PDFs, LCDAs, and decay constants of the vector meson in the Schwinger model for several fermion masses. States in Hilbert space are efficiently represented by tensor networks, with an expressivity that is systematically controlled by a bond dimension. The light-front Wilson line is implemented as a stepwise evolution on the lattice that alternates spatial shifts of an external charge with Trotterized time-evolution steps acting on a matrix product state. All systematic uncertainties are quantified by varying and extrapolating in the lattice spacing, volume, bond dimension, gauge-field truncation, and Trotter step width. The slow growth of the entanglement entropy makes moderate bond dimensions sufficient, which supports the feasibility of using tensor networks for computing light-front matrix elements in more general settings. We confirm that the computed distributions fulfill the expected normalizations, momentum sum rules, and symmetry properties.
item.dc:creator: Mari Carmen Ba\~nuls, Krzysztof Cichy, C. -J. David Lin, Manuel Schneider

item.title: SPARK: Spectral Preconditioned Analytic Residual Kolmogorov Arnold Networks for incompressible Navier Stokes equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.31834v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose Spectral Jet KAN (SJ-KAN) to reduce the cost of differentiation and the network complexity of Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) for the Navier-Stokes (NS) equations. The input coordinates are embedded through Chebyshev bases whose spatial derivatives are known in closed form, and all differentiation matrices are computed once for the collocation points before training. A single linear layer compresses the Chebyshev bases into a few latent features, and a single nonlinear Chebyshev Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (CKAN) layer maps these features to the physical variables. Because the basis derivatives are known in advance and the compression is linear, the spatial derivatives in the NS equations are carried through the network analytically by a fixed sequence of matrix products and elementwise operations. Automatic differentiation (AD) is used only in backpropagation, to compute the gradients of the loss with respect to the network weights. We examine three variants of SJ-KAN (JetKAN, JetKAN-F, JetKAN-H), which differ in how the output layer maps the latent features to the physical variables. All variants are tested on the Taylor-Green vortex and on the lid driven cavity at Reynolds numbers Re = 100, 1000, 5000 and 10,000. The results are compared with a KAN that uses AD (PIKAN) and with a standard PINN. The SJ-KAN variants reach comparable or better accuracy than both, with up to 47 times fewer parameters and up to 8.2 times faster training per epoch. SJ-KAN also solves the lid driven cavity flow at Re = 10,000 without any reference data and with fewer than 9,000 trainable parameters. These results show that analytic derivative propagation, a small spectral input layer and a single KAN layer give a faster and simpler solver than methods based on AD, also for flows at high Reynolds numbers.
item.dc:creator: Dathi Rajasekhar, Thien-Tam Nguyen, Trung Bao Le

item.title: OMNI-P3x universal neural network potential for large-scale computational photochemistry workflows
item.description: arXiv:2611.32133v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Computational photochemistry supports the design and understanding of new materials. However, the high cost of excited-state quantum-mechanical (QM) calculations makes screening large molecular libraries prohibitively expensive. To address this limitation, we introduce OMNI-P3x, a universal machine-learned interatomic potential (MLIP) for singlet ground- and excited-state simulations of neutral and charged organic molecules. Trained on both ground- and excited-state conformations, it performs complete computational photochemistry workflows with accuracy approaching TD-DFT. We demonstrate its practical applicability by screening a combinatorial library of 234,375 flavylium derivatives, where the pretrained model performs ground-state geometry optimization and predicts absorption properties without additional QM calculations. Following fine-tuning, we further screen 162,960 xanthene-based dyes, identifying new candidates for red, near-infrared and short-wavelength infrared emission. Furthermore, state-dependent neural charges, learned without reference atomic charges, provide an interpretable picture of intramolecular charge redistribution upon excitation.
item.dc:creator: Miko{\l}aj Martyka, Joanna Jankowska, Pavlo O. Dral

item.title: Augmented Imaginary-Time Evolution of Neural Quantum States with Implicit Time Steps
item.description: arXiv:2611.32236v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Finding the ground states of quantum many-body systems remains a central challenge in physics and quantum chemistry. Imaginary-time evolution (ITE) offers a natural, widely used route, but its convergence is typically asymptotic. Variational approaches restrict this evolution to parameterized manifolds, with neural quantum states (NQS) providing flexible representations commonly optimized via stochastic reconfiguration (SR). Their performance depends on the geometry of the variational manifold, the convergence properties of ITE, and the stability of finite-step explicit (forward) integrators. By exploiting local geometric information of the energy landscape, the recently introduced augmented imaginary-time evolution (AITE) can, in principle, reach the ground state in finite imaginary time. To exploit the accelerated convergence of AITE in NQS optimization, we first combine an implicit Euler step with Galerkin projection to derive an implicit SR scheme that permits large, stable steps and substantially outperforms conventional methods. We use it to formulate an implicit version of AITE and show that its acceleration persists under variational projection and finite-step integration with asymptotically quadratic convergence of the energy error. With finite sampling, implicit schemes yield consistent gains, and implicit AITE becomes increasingly advantageous.
item.dc:creator: Maksymilian Kliczkowski, Thomas D. K\"uhne, Fedor \v{S}imkovic IV, Prachi Sharma, Carlos L. Benavides-Riveros, Werner Dobrautz

item.title: Thermodynamics of complex crystals from a generalized mean-field bond model
item.description: arXiv:2611.32609v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We extend our previously introduced mean-field bond model from unary fcc lattices to crystals with multiple chemical species and sublattices, accurately predicting finite-temperature thermodynamics without statistical sampling. Our generalization reformulates the model in terms of the Wyckoff positions of the crystal, representing each by one atom, and solving for the bond density of the reference bond of each of its neighbor shells. Bond-bond correlation functions are built from the zero-temperature force constants, allowing the deviation of every bond in the crystal to be expressed through linear functions of the reference bond of a shell. Thermodynamic self-consistency is enforced by requiring a single virial temperature for the whole crystal, and compatibility of average bond lengths with crystal volume. Model predictions are validated against molecular dynamics simulations of unary, binary, and ternary crystals using Morse-type bonding potentials, parametrized for each shell from the force constants of empirical interatomic potentials at several isotropic strains. In each case, the predicted bond densities and thermodynamics agree with the simulations to within their statistical uncertainty. We discuss strategies for combining the model with bonding potentials parametrized from first principles and foundation models to predict the finite-temperature thermodynamics of complex crystals at ab initio accuracy without statistical sampling.
item.dc:creator: Raynol Dsouza, Thomas D. Swinburne, J\"org Neugebauer

item.title: Mixing and Preserving Properties of Non-van der Waals 2D Materials in Sandwich-like Heterostructures
item.description: arXiv:2611.32723v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Heterostructure interfaces created by stacking two-dimensional (2D) materials outline an appealing route towards achieving advanced electronic and magnetic functionalities at the nanoscale. Non-van der Waals (non-vdW) sandwich-like heterostructures (HSs) are build out of non-vdW 2D materials derived from non-layered crystals and establish a new frontier enabling strong interfacial coupling. Employing ab initio density functional theory (DFT), we investigate two classes of such trilayer HSs: purely non-vdW assemblies and hybrid vdW/non-vdW/vdW stacks. We show that non-vdW sandwiches undergo pronounced geometric reconstruction forming chemically bonded interfaces with large absolute binding energies up to an order of magnitude larger than those of conventional vdW HSs. These strong interactions drive extensive electronic hybridization, band gap renormalization, and tunable interlayer magnetic coupling. In contrast, vdW encapsulation largely protects the intrinsic atomic and electronic structure of the non-vdW sheet from the environment , while enabling charge transfer doping of the vdW layers. Our results thus establish sandwich HSs a versatile interface design platform, spanning interaction regimes from weakly perturbed encapsulation to strongly interacting chemically bonded systems with emergent electronic and magnetic behavior.
item.dc:creator: Anastasiia Nihei, Rico Friedrich

item.title: Packing the Bragg sphere: complete three-dimensional photonic band gaps at the refractive index of polymers (1.55)
item.description: arXiv:2611.32789v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Complete 3D photonic band gaps have so far been found only at refractive-index contrasts of about 1.9 and above, reached by rod-connected diamond lattice structures. Reciprocal-space design of quasiperiodic structures recently achieved considerable emission attenuation at much lower contrasts [L. Maiwald et al., Adv. Optical Mater. 10, 2100785 (2022)]. Here we implement systematic search and reciprocal-space design of periodic 3D structures with complete band gaps, solving a discrete optimization problem on an integer lattice. A gap above a high band needs the strongest Fourier components of the dielectric close to the Bragg sphere of that band. Crystals with large cells, started from Fourier peaks at the vertices of a polyhedron on this sphere and optimized against densely refined band edges, open complete gaps down to an index contrast of 1.55, that of common polymers against air. A rational approximant of an icosidodecahedron gave the most efficient location of the Fourier peaks among the polyhedra tested. Numerical calculations confirm the gaps over a resolution series, with band edges searched over the whole Brillouin zone. The best designs are connected porous networks, suited to a microwave test with printed polymer. A rigorous bound, valid for any structure, does not exclude gaps at lower index, and the next rational approximants of the icosidodecahedron, whose Bragg zones match bands 576 and 2440 almost exactly, point to where gaps at even lower contrast may be sought.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Itin

item.title: Path-probability gradients for optimizing force fields against dynamical observables
item.description: arXiv:2611.32851v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Machine learning force fields inherit the errors of the electronic-structure methods used to generate their training data, and refining them against experimental measurements provides a direct route beyond this limit. However, such refinement remains difficult for dynamical observables because differentiating chaotic molecular trajectories yields unstable gradients. Here, we introduce PathGrad, which differentiates Langevin path probabilities instead of the trajectories themselves. The resulting gradient estimator is accumulated on the fly from thermal noise and force derivatives, and its variance remains stable as the trajectory length increases. We validated the gradient estimator against finite-difference calculations and used it to fine-tune molten-copper and water potentials against experimental diffusion coefficients together with structural constraints. For water, jointly optimizing diffusion and the oxygen-oxygen radial distribution function also improves the predictions of shear viscosity and rotational relaxation, neither of which is included in the optimization objective. Alignment at a single temperature also improves the apparent activation energies of multiple dynamical observables, bringing their temperature dependences closer to experiments. Moreover, the optimized potential exhibits smaller force errors relative to an independent, higher-level quantum-chemical reference, indicating that alignment with experiments improves the fidelity of the potential energy surface beyond the fitted targets. PathGrad thus establishes a general framework for incorporating experimental observables directly into force field optimizations.
item.dc:creator: Zhongyao Wang, Lun Song, Yakun Zeng, Xingao Gong, Rui Shi, Mao Su

item.title: From Fermions to Vortices: Microscopic Simulations of Phase Ordering in a d-Wave Superconductor
item.description: arXiv:2611.32916v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Describing bath-induced superconducting phase ordering directly from a microscopic fermionic Hamiltonian remains a formidable challenge. Here we develop a microscopic framework for this problem using the recently introduced adiabatic variational principle (AVP) and demonstrate its application to a two-dimensional $d$-wave superconductor. The central construction maps evolving, spatially inhomogeneous bond-pairing fields onto constrained Bogoliubov-de Gennes states, with the associated Lagrange multipliers determining the thermodynamic driving forces. This enables dissipative evolution of the superconducting order while retaining its microscopic electronic structure, without assuming a phenomenological Ginzburg-Landau free-energy functional. Starting from disordered pairing configurations, we resolve the emergence of phase coherence through vortex-antivortex annihilation and the accompanying evolution of local electronic spectra. Vortex decay and dynamical scaling recover the characteristic kinetics of two-dimensional phase ordering, providing a nontrivial benchmark of the framework. The solver-independent AVP formulation opens a route to microscopic studies of dissipative ordering and metastability in superconductors with intertwined stripe and pair-density-wave orders.
item.dc:creator: Ali Rayat, Gia-Wei Chern

item.title: Parametric neural-network wavefunctions across a bosonic phase transition
item.description: arXiv:2611.33150v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose Boseformer, a universal attention-based neural-network architecture for representing the wavefunctions of particles with bosonic quantum statistics, including superfluid and crystal phases. The model is trained to generate the wavefunction as a function of a Hamiltonian parameter across the quantum phase transition between these phases. Once trained with variational Monte Carlo optimization, it can serve as a foundation model describing the phase transition without the need to retrain it for individual parameter values. We demonstrate our method on a system of two-dimensional bosons with $1/r^3$ repulsive interaction.
item.dc:creator: Daniil S. Antonenko, Liang Fu, Leonid I. Glazman

item.title: Simulation of S-parameters of general multilayer boxed PCBs with the method of moments and the scattering matrix algorithm
item.description: arXiv:2605.18492v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper addresses the problem of modeling high-frequency parameters for shielded printed circuit boards (PCBs) using the Green's function for a multilayer waveguide and the S-matrix formalism. The proposed approach incorporates a simple, intuitive method for calculating the full tensor Green's function. The corresponding matrix elements are described using three sets of S-matrices associated with the dielectric layers of the PCB substrate. The method of moments (MoM) is implemented using surface "roof-top" functions, as well as volumetric pulse and linear basis functions; all overlap integrals involving these functions and the waveguide modes are derived in explicit form, enabling the efficient modeling of both planar metallization layers and vertical interconnects. To accelerate computations, a new approach to deriving the expansion of the MoM matrix elements is proposed, which facilitates the application of the fast Fourier transform.
item.dc:creator: A. O. Makarenko, P. Zheglova, R. Gaponenko, R. V. Salimov, R. I. Tikhonov, A. A. Shcherbakov

item.title: High-level, efficient ocean modeling at all scales with Oceananigans
item.description: arXiv:2502.14148v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We describe the user interface, governing equations, and numerical methods underpinning the ocean modeling software called "Oceananigans". Oceananigans development has been led by the Climate Modeling Alliance as part of a larger effort to build a trainable climate model with quantifiable uncertainty. Notably, Oceananigans is written in the Julia programming language, is optimized for GPUs, and can efficiently simulate all scales of ocean motion ranging from millimeter-scale turbulence in a small box to planetary-scale ocean circulation. We argue that a reusable finite-volume framework on structured staggered grids, GPU-efficient algorithms, and accessible interfaces and source code together enable efficient all-scale simulations and rapid innovation in model development. This design negotiates a dual mandate for highest-possible performance (to support state-of-the-art applications) and enhanced accessibility (to facilitate adoption and development). The dual mandate aims ultimately to accelerate the progress of Earth system science.
item.dc:creator: Gregory L. Wagner, Simone Silvestri, Navid C. Constantinou, Ali Ramadhan, Jean-Michel Campin, Chris Hill, Tom\'as Chor, Jago Strong-Wright, Xin Kai Lee, Francis Poulin, Andre Souza, Keaton J. Burns, Siddhartha Bishnu, John Marshall, Raffaele Ferrari

item.title: Inner sublattice competition: a minimal mechanism for reentrant localizations in Aubry-Andr\'e lattice
item.description: arXiv:2606.24720v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct a double mosaic Aubry-Andr\'e (DMAA) model with two independent quasiperiodic potentials assigned to corresponding even and odd sublattices of the AA lattice, and show that the competition between them gives rise to multiple localization-delocalization transitions under single-parameter tuning. Such reentrant localizations are verified by comprehensive numerical characterizations including the inverse participation ratio, normalized participation ratio, fractal dimension, and real-space wavefunction distributions. Simulations based on a continuous polariton model yield consistent results, confirming the experimental feasibility of the predicted phenomena. This inner sublattice competition mechanism works in a minimal way for reentrant localizations without additional ingredients or dynamical modifications such as long-range hopping, mixed quasiperiodic and random disorder, or non-Hermitian gain and loss, offering a concise route to engineer reentrant localization based on the canonical AA lattice family.
item.dc:creator: Hangdong Qiu, Yunhua Wang

item.title: ZStar: A unified toolkit for polarization, Born effective charges, dielectric and piezoelectric responses, and infrared and Raman spectra
item.description: arXiv:2609.16802v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Polarization and the response to atomic displacements determine the dielectric, piezoelectric, and vibrational spectroscopy of materials, yet these quantities are usually obtained through separate workflows within ABACUS. Here, we present ZStar, an open-source Python toolkit that unifies these calculations. Using ABACUS and PYATB, ZStar derives Born effective charges (BECs) and zone-center force constants from one symmetry-adapted displacement set, and reuses the displaced electronic matrices for Raman spectra. Berry phases in periodic directions combined with charge-density dipoles in nonperiodic directions extend the method from bulk crystals (3D) to 2D and 1D materials and molecules (0D). These BECs and phonon modes give infrared intensities and the lattice contribution to the dielectric response. From finite strains, ZStar further obtains clamped-ion and relaxed-ion piezoelectric coefficients. This unified workflow reduces the computational cost by up to 4.2$\times$ for BECs and zone-center phonons and 8.4$\times$ for combined infrared and Raman calculations. ZStar also supports machine-learned models by generating training data and post-processing prediction results into physical properties.
item.dc:creator: Xudong Zhu, Junhong Li, Gan Jin, Zheng Guan, Meng Zhang, Lixin He

item.title: Winding-Pack Quench Simulation of Stellarator Coils: Hydraulic Field-Network Coupling and Transverse Heat Conduction in OPENSC$^2$
item.description: arXiv:2611.08084v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Quench propagation in cable-in-conduit conductors is thermo-hydraulically driven, yet a standalone 1D model treats a conductor as one straight adiabatic cable with prescribed pressure and mass-flow boundaries, so secondary quenches and flow redistribution between windings cannot be resolved without coupling to further, so far proprietary, codes. We extend the open-source code OPENSC$^2$ with transverse heat conduction between turns, a 3D field resolving the current-sharing temperature, induced losses, and a lumped hydraulic network coupled to the conductors by a mass-flow formulation. Compared to the 2006 W7-X coil tests, it predicts the quench site and cuts the outlet-temperature overestimation from 55 K to 25 K. The identified mechanisms indicate that the position of the helium inlets and outlets relative to the field, the hydraulic interconnection of the windings, the turn insulation and the current dump should be considered together in the quench design of future stellarator coils.
item.dc:creator: Laura A. M. D'Angelo, Felix Warmer

item.title: Gutzwiller Quantum-Classical Embedding for Dynamics Simulations of Correlated Electron Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.24592v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Simulating the real-time dynamics of correlated electron systems requires a nonperturbative treatment of local correlations over long times, a challenge for classical methods. We present the time-dependent Gutzwiller quantum-classical embedding framework, t-GQCE, for generic multi-orbital lattice models with time-dependent Hamiltonians. Within the time-dependent ghost Gutzwiller approximation, a noninteracting quasiparticle lattice propagated classically is coupled to finite interacting embedding models propagated on quantum processors. The two parts exchange only embedding Hamiltonian parameters and single-particle density matrices, and the framework is agnostic to the quantum solver. We demonstrate it with adaptive variational quantum dynamics simulations of interaction quenches in the Hubbard model on the Bethe lattice. Without ghost orbitals, the embedding problem reduces to a single qubit, simulated on IBM quantum hardware with an ancilla qubit. With ghost orbitals, t-GQCE suppresses the artificial undamped oscillations of the conventional Gutzwiller approximation and approaches nonequilibrium dynamical mean-field theory results for weak and strong quenches. Statevector simulations with 2 to 6 ghost orbitals per spin, or 8 to 16 qubits, give adaptive circuits that follow the embedding states with infidelities below $5\times10^{-4}$. Under trapped-ion noise models, circuit compression, measurements in rotated orbital bases with post-selection, and noise mitigation reduce the errors two- to threefold. At one third of the error rates of a hardware-benchmarked noise model, they reach an absolute accuracy of $0.01$ for all single-particle density matrix elements and the double occupancy with $10^5$ shots per time step, and the Quantinuum H2-Emulator gives similar accuracy, suggesting that t-GQCE is a viable approach for early fault-tolerant quantum processors.
item.dc:creator: Joshua Aftergood, Daniele Guerci, Jacob Brunton, Feng Zhang, Thomas Iadecola, Peter P. Orth, Cai-Zhuang Wang, Nicola Lanat\`a, Yong-Xin Yao
